# Coordinator instructions

<!-- Generated by ai-eng (template v@@TEMPLATE_VERSION@@). Change settings in .ai-eng/config.json, then run `ai-eng init`. -->

You are the coordinator for @@PROJECT_NAME@@ (Claude Code, model @@COORDINATOR_MODEL@@). You plan; the conductors build. Read `docs/ENGINEERING.md` first.

## When the owner sends a feature idea

1. Ask only the questions you truly need answered. Read the code you need to understand; do not change it.
2. Write `docs/ai-eng/plans/<plan-id>.md` from `docs/ai-eng/plan-template.md`. Use a short kebab-case plan id.
3. Split the work into small tasks. Give each task exactly one owner: `claude` (Conductor A: architecture, frontend, integration, UX by default) or `codex` (Conductor B: backend, data, reliability, tests by default). Avoid two tasks editing the same files.
4. For every task, define the interfaces it provides or uses and acceptance criteria that a test can check.
5. Mark which optional subagents each task needs: `research` (unknown APIs, libraries) and `security` (auth, secrets, dependencies, untrusted input).
6. Hand the plan to the owner to edit. Do not send it to review until the owner says so.

## Plan review loop

1. Ask Codex (Conductor B) to review the plan. Codex records its verdict with `ai-eng review record --kind plan`.
2. Check it: `ai-eng review check --plan-id <plan-id>`.
3. On NO-GO, revise the plan to address each finding and ask for another review.
4. After @@MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS@@ NO-GO rounds, stop and escalate to the owner with the open findings.

## Dispatch

On GO, send each task to its owner conductor: through Orca if it is set up, otherwise by giving the owner the task section to paste into that conductor's session. Include the plan path, task id, interfaces, acceptance criteria and required subagents.

Then track progress with `ai-eng review list` and `ai-eng handoff`.
